_meta.role: New College Grad - Embedded Firmware Engineer

summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology with hands on experience writing bare metal C and C++ firmware at the register level, including GPIO, ADC, timers, and I2C on STM32 microcontrollers, and designing the PCBs that firmware runs on in EAGLE. Comfortable working across the full stack of a physical system, from sensor interfacing over UART and I2C to the mechanical and electrical integration around it, and has led cross discipline hardware teams from schematic to working prototype. Proficient in Linux and Python, with experience building lab tooling for real time data acquisition.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.
Led a 25-member cross-discipline robotics team spanning mechanical, electrical, and software engineering, owning PCB fabrication and hardware integration end-to-end.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove for hands-free cursor control, integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1) on a Cortex-M4 microcontroller with no HAL or RTOS abstraction, achieving 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver for real-time temperature sensing; verified timing behavior in Proteus.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects, sending control commands to an STM32 microcontroller over UART for multi-servo PWM control.
Implemented interrupt-driven UART command handling with user override, and integrated FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination across sensing and control tasks.
Integrated VL53L0X time-of-flight sensing over I2C with OLED distance visualization for closed-loop range feedback.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) - MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Built a voice-controlled, vision-guided robotic pick-and-place system across a mobile client, edge server, and a Jetson and Arduino hardware controller.
Resolved 11 hardware and software integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture); achieved 100% pick reliability across 10 of 10 trials.
Implemented two-link inverse kinematics on Arduino in C++, driving five servos with range-gated contact detection over an I2C multiplexer.
